Yes — the closest match is a multimodal fact-checking system that uses both text and visual evidence, and one paper explicitly argues for adaptively using visual evidence only when it helps verification. VILLAIN verifies image-text claims through multi-agent collaboration and produces a verdict from the claim plus retrieved evidence [1]. AMuFC specifically studies visual evidence necessity and shows that indiscriminate use of visual evidence can reduce accuracy, proposing adaptive use instead [7].

If you want a system that decides whether an image is useful or harmful for verification, [7] is the best fit; [1] is broader claim verification rather than explicit usefulness/harmfulness gating.
